requirement_results.command: comparing a release with itself is IDENTICAL with a stable content-addressed digest; comparing two distinct releases in reverse order yields a different digest, since the diff is directional (added vs removed)
a candidate release with an added, a removed and a changed resource relative to its predecessor produces a distinct structural diff digest

identical releases classify IDENTICAL; a pure resource addition classifies COMPATIBLE; a resource removal, a field's type declaration being removed, and an existing field's declared type changing all classify BREAKING
a migration plan is deterministic (repeated calls produce byte-identical plans, including their own plan_digest) and content-addressed; a differently-shaped candidate produces a different plan_digest
generate() produces a single release-manifest ArtifactManifestEntry whose digest is a real content-addressed SHA-256 URN over the release's own resource identities
a BREAKING candidate cannot reach generate_governed() without an explicit, non-empty governed migration plan -- the negative acceptance criterion, made executable
a BREAKING candidate accompanied by its own real, non-empty migration plan (produced by RetainedMigrationPlanner) reaches generation successfully
a COMPATIBLE candidate reaches generation even with no migration plan at all
a blocked BREAKING generation attempt (even with a migration plan present but empty of steps) never returns any artifact list, partial or otherwise

full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing; a transient Fuseki OOM was diagnosed and resolved by restarting only that service, confirmed unrelated to this task's own changes)

residual_risks: The compatibility classification's BREAKING/COMPATIBLE rules cover exactly the invariants this task's own new grammar (OCOR-DEV-0032's field_types/resources) can express -- resource removal and field-type removal/change; a richer future grammar (e.g. nested types, cardinality) would need its own dedicated classification rules, not a claim this task makes.

generate_governed()'s migration-plan check only requires the plan to be non-empty (at least one migration step) and does not independently re-verify the plan's own plan_digest against a freshly recomputed one -- a caller supplying a forged or stale plan object with a non-empty migration_steps list would still pass; this matches the task's own smallest-contract-compliant scope (the negative acceptance criterion is about the PRESENCE of a governed migration plan, not yet about independently re-verifying its authenticity, which is a C6/Decision-gate concern outside C1's scope).

generate() itself (the sealed ArtifactGenerator Protocol method) is deliberately unconditional, exactly matching its sealed signature (release: CanonicalIrRelease) -> ...; generate_governed() is the new, additional method this task introduces to make the negative acceptance criterion executable without changing the sealed Protocol's own contract.

A transient, unrelated Fuseki OOM (documented as a recurring finding throughout this session, caused by an unrelated large host container sharing the same Docker daemon) produced 15 errors on the first regression attempt; resolved by restarting only the Fuseki service, confirmed unrelated to this task via a clean second regression run.
